units.translation: ⟦1⟧ also at 475, 678. The scholiast, who had the corrupt text, understands it completely wrongly: you who are ugly will not be able to revile me again; but even if one writes ⟦2⟧ and makes ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧ the object, then with the epithet exactly what should not happen occurs. Also in Aeschylus only ⟦5⟧ is found (504, ⟦6⟧, ⟦7⟧), not, as in others, also ⟦8⟧.

On ⟦1⟧ cf. especially Frg. 156 ⟦2⟧ (⟦3⟧) ⟦4⟧, and 287 ⟦5⟧. — Athena appears in this whole speech as completely humanized with regard to knowledge; as indeed could hardly be otherwise, if she was to appear as a character in the drama; her fine impartiality and consideration toward the Erinyes contrasts with Apollo's behavior and manner of speaking; but he is also a party to the case. Cf. Introduction p. 6.
but Persuasion stands aloof from the gods
a god does not stand aloof from just deceit
Stichomythia 415–435, again (as at 198) introduced with 3 verses.

416 ⟦1⟧ as at 479, 943 (⟦2⟧) lugubris, cf. ⟦3⟧ 940, also Pindar several times, and already Archilochus Frg. 38 (⟦4⟧, which is explained with ⟦5⟧); imitating it Sophocles in Ajax 673 ⟦6⟧. The spelling varies in Aeschylus between ⟦7⟧ and ⟦8⟧, in Sophocles between ⟦9⟧ and ⟦10⟧; but the form ⟦11⟧ has no authority, see Dindorf. Different is ⟦12⟧ "eternal" at V. 572 (cf. 672), which seems to be connected with ⟦13⟧, as the other word with ⟦14⟧. –
⟦1⟧: cf. ⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧, and Introduction p. 2; in this name the thought indeed seems to show clearly through the mythical veil (cf. ⟦4⟧ [Paley]).
418 ⟦1⟧ I have now learned. I await further.
⟦1⟧ is otherwise always "named after something" or "corresponding to its name" 90, ⟦2⟧ etc., cf. ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧; so here too "corresponding to the dark descent from Night".
